result.paraphrase: The emergence of Internet of Things (IoT) technology has transformed existing medical devices into smart tools for creating a health-related digital world. IoT offers great promise in electronic health (e-health), where current technologies are deployed to provide fast access to patient care. IoT-based e-health systems use major technologies and connected objects to monitor, identify, track, manage, and store patient information for continuous healthcare. For successful IoT deployment in e-health, a mechanism is needed that guarantees interoperability among devices so resources can be processed and used efficiently. The study introduces a distinctive concept by exclusively incorporating an e-governance layer into the design and implementation of IoT-based e-health systems. Accordingly, it aims to develop a new architecture for integrating IoT into e-health systems by focusing deeply on its sensing, application, transmission, fog, and e-governance layers to enable quick response, secure transmission, and improved healthcare services. An exploratory study was conducted to examine the existing literature on cutting-edge developments in e-health. The proposed IoT-based e-health architecture is highly novel and comprehensive, with the inclusion of a very crucial but previously overlooked component of Emergency Medical Services (EMS), integrated through blockchain technology. Another novelty is the explicit definition of the e-governance layer that encompasses all layers of the proposed architecture to achieve quality healthcare services.
